boards.title: Your First Weekend at Saint Louis University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-stakes, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to SLU’s campus, finding useful student spaces, and ending with a recurring campus connection.

cards.title: Start with a campus reset on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Find the central green space
cards.notes: Walk the Quad first to orient yourself between nearby buildings. Bring a blanket or simply pause there before choosing the rest of your route.
cards.short_summary: Use the central lawn as your first visual anchor for the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU identifies the Quad as a campus spot for spreading out a blanket, studying, or playing pickup Frisbee.
cards.source_title: Saint Louis University's St. Louis Campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; check campus conditions and event setup when you arrive.

cards.title: Say hello to the Billiken
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Drury Rally Plaza outside Chaifetz Arena
cards.notes: Stop at the bronze statue for a first-weekend photo and, if it suits you, take part in the documented good-luck belly-rub tradition.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark tied to SLU’s Billiken identity.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU says the bronze Billiken statue is in Drury Rally Plaza outside Chaifetz Arena and that its plaque describes rubbing its belly for good luck.
cards.source_title: You're in Luck: The History of SLU's Billiken Statue
cards.access_notes: The statue is outdoors at Drury Rally Plaza; be mindful of arena-event crowds.

cards.title: Make your first campus meal a sit-down one
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Grand Hall
cards.notes: Use Grand Dining Hall to get familiar with residential dining and its posted dietary options. Check the current menu or meal-plan access before going.
cards.short_summary: A practical first meal stop with multiple dining stations.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU lists Grand Dining Hall among its campus dining locations and describes it as an all-you-care-to-eat venue with eight dining stations.
cards.access_notes: Meal-plan or other payment access may be required; consult DineSLU for current service details.

cards.title: Locate your campus hub
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 20 N. Grand Blvd.
cards.notes: Walk through the BSC to locate the information desk, Student Involvement Center, prayer space, meeting areas, and dining choices for future use.
cards.short_summary: A central building for student services, organizations, and everyday needs.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU describes Busch Student Center as a campus hub with student-development offices, student organizations, dining, meeting spaces, and an interfaith prayer space.
cards.access_notes: SLU lists regular building hours as 7 a.m.–12 a.m.; individual offices and vendors may differ.

cards.title: Pick a study spot before classes begin
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 3650 Lindell Blvd.
cards.notes: Take a short scouting lap through Pius and note a seat, room, or service you may use later. Save the library help contact for research questions.
cards.short_summary: A large campus library with study seating and academic support resources.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU states that Pius XII Memorial Library has 1,600 seats, 48 study rooms, public computers, and 24-hour access Sunday through Friday during fall and spring semesters.
cards.access_notes: SLU reports 24-hour access Sunday–Friday in fall and spring semesters; verify current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Take the self-guided historic-house tour
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · 3673 West Pine Mall
cards.notes: Visit during listed public hours and use the self-guided tour book to explore the house. Confirm hours first because they can change during holiday breaks.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-guided look inside a historic campus house.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU says Samuel Cupples House is open Tuesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m., offers self-guided tours, and has free admission.
cards.access_notes: Individual visits are listed Tuesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; hours may change during holiday breaks.

cards.title: Try a drop-in recreation option
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Central campus
cards.notes: Bring your SLU ID and choose one simple activity, such as a swim, indoor track walk, or court time. Check the facility schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility with several indoor activity options.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU describes Simon Recreation Center as a 120,000-square-foot facility with a pool, courts, bouldering wall, fitness center, spinning studio, and indoor track; students are automatic members.
cards.access_notes: SLU students are automatic members and must use their SLU ID for access; verify current facility hours and activity availability.

cards.title: Pause at College Church
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Campus worship space
cards.notes: If you would like a reflective stop, visit College Church or plan around a listed service. Its schedule includes student-focused Sunday evening Masses in the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A historic on-campus church that serves SLU and the parish community.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU identifies St. Francis Xavier College Church as a worship space for the University and parish community and says Campus Ministry runs 4:30 p.m. and 8 p.m. Sunday Masses during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Service times vary by academic calendar; consult the current Mass schedule before attending.

cards.title: Find the arena before game day
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Campus athletics landmark
cards.notes: Walk by Chaifetz Arena and note its location near the Billiken statue. Later, use the official athletics schedule to decide whether a game fits your calendar.
cards.short_summary: SLU’s home venue for basketball and volleyball.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU identifies Chaifetz Arena as the 10,600-seat home of its men’s and women’s basketball teams and volleyball team.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is separate from event entry; check the official athletics schedule and event ticket terms for access.

cards.title: Put the next SLU Fair on your calendar
cards.subtitle: Sunday evening · Student-organization activity
cards.notes: Browse SLU Groups now, then attend the next semester’s SLU Fair to talk directly with organizations. Use it to identify one follow-up meeting or event.
cards.short_summary: A recurring semester activity for discovering active student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: SLU states that SLU Fair is held each semester and showcases nearly all active clubs and organizations on campus.
cards.access_notes: SLU says the fair occurs each semester; check SLU Groups or campus communications for the current date and location.
